hero.title: SDET Career – Present & Future
hero.subtitle: Understand the role, the industry, and where it's heading

whatIsSdet.heading: What is an SDET?
whatIsSdet.body: A Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) is not just a tester — they are a software engineer who specialises in quality. An SDET writes automation code, designs test frameworks, validates complex systems, and ensures software is production-ready at scale. They sit at the intersection of development and quality, and are expected to think like a developer while owning the reliability of the product.

points.title: Automation First
points.desc: Write robust, maintainable automation code — not just manual test cases.

points.title: End-to-End Thinking
points.desc: Understand and test across UI, APIs, microservices, and databases.

points.title: Framework Design
points.desc: Design scalable test frameworks that teams can build on top of.

points.title: Risk Identification
points.desc: Identify critical paths, edge cases, and production risks before release.

points.title: Engineering Mindset
points.desc: Collaborate with developers, contribute to CI/CD, and treat tests as code.

tools.name: Selenium
tools.desc: Selenium remains the backbone of enterprise automation. It has a massive ecosystem, supports all major languages, and is deeply integrated into legacy and large-scale systems. If you work in a bank, insurance company, or any large organisation, Selenium is very likely in their stack.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.desc: Playwright is the modern choice. Built by Microsoft, it is faster, more reliable, and aligned with how today's web works. It handles dynamic content, network interception, and multi-browser testing out of the box. Playwright is where the industry is actively moving.

points.title: API & Microservices Testing
points.desc: The shift is clear — UI testing alone is not enough. API and service-level testing is becoming the core skill of modern SDETs.

points.title: AI-Assisted Testing
points.desc: AI is entering test generation, failure analysis, and intelligent assertions. SDETs who can use AI tools will have a massive productivity advantage.

points.title: Speed & Stability Focus
points.desc: Flaky tests and slow pipelines are being eliminated. The focus is on fast, deterministic, and intelligent validation.

points.title: Playwright & AI Integration
points.desc: Playwright's modern architecture, programmatic control, and flexible APIs make it highly compatible with AI-assisted workflows — a key reason it is gaining industry momentum.

advice.title: Master One Tool First
advice.desc: Go deep into either Selenium or Playwright. Build real projects, understand the internals, and get confident.

advice.title: Learn the Other Tool Too
advice.desc: Once you're strong in one, pick up the other. Flexibility across both tools makes you valuable in any team or company.

advice.title: Build API Automation Skills
advice.desc: REST Assured, Playwright API, or Axios — API testing is non-negotiable for a modern SDET.

advice.title: Design a Framework
advice.desc: Don't just write tests. Learn Page Object Model, reporting, CI/CD integration, and modular design.

advice.title: Use AI as a Productivity Tool
advice.desc: Use GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, or similar tools to write tests faster, debug smarter, and learn quicker.

closing.text: We cover both Selenium and Playwright in this platform to help you build a strong foundation and stay future-ready as an SDET.
